sonnet.problem: This card asks for the name of the man at the king's gate. Card 1 already says Mordecai is at the gate, and cards 2 and 3 name him again. The blank is answered by the cards before it, so it re-asks a fact the baker has already been told.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The true statement bundles several claims: asking the king in the morning, having Mordecai hanged, and going to the banquet to enjoy himself. It also says "Zeresh and his friends" before Haman is named, so "his" has no clear referent when the baker reads it.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.
